name: SpeechGPT: Empowering Large Language Models with Intrinsic Cross-Modal Conversational Abilities
problem: Cascaded speech systems (ASR -> text -> LLM -> TTS) cannot transfer knowledge between modalities, so speech understanding degrades relative to text.
mechanism: Builds the SpeechInstruct cross-modal instruction dataset and trains with a three-stage strategy: modality-adaptation pre-training, then cross-modal instruction fine-tuning, then chain-of-modality instruction fine-tuning. Modality-specific input/output units are wrapped as discrete tokens and mixed into the LLM token stream.
notes:
arXiv preprint, self-described 'work in progress'; no peer-reviewed venue found. Do not treat the speech-LM cluster as production: SpeechGPT, SALMONN and Audio Flamingo are research artifacts whose checkpoints are demo-scale. The architectural lesson for inference is the token-rate issue again - representing speech as discrete units in the LLM token stream means audio length becomes LLM sequence length, so token rate is the dominant cost knob, and none of these papers report a hardware-level throughput comparison.
